intro:
What does "quantum" mean here?

There is no need to make "quantum" complicated. It means the smallest possible packet of energy — one that cannot be divided further. The packet of light in particular is called a photon.

Standing by a window warms you; sunlight on your skin makes vitamin D. Light is not only brightness — it does real work inside the body. Photosynthesis, by which plants make nutrients from sunlight, and the way migratory birds sense the Earth's magnetic field to find their way, are both described in the international literature as phenomena involving these very small packets of energy. The field is called quantum biology.

Our Quantum care programme applies only those parts of it for which clinical research in humans has accumulated sufficiently.

How does light wake a cell?

Inside the cells of the body are tiny power stations called mitochondria. The energy they produce is called ATP — put simply, the battery a cell runs on. With age or exhaustion these power stations lose performance, and recovery slows down accordingly.

  1. Light of a specific wavelengthis delivered through the skin.
  2. Mitochondriathe power stations inside the cell absorb it.
  3. ATP (the cell's battery)energy production increases.
  4. Resultthe processes of recovery and regeneration are supported.

When light of a particular wavelength reaches the body, a component inside the mitochondria called cytochrome c oxidase absorbs it. A substance that normally hinders energy production sits on that component, and the packets of light detach it. The brake, so to speak, is released.

The power station then returns to its proper speed, ATP production rises, and the signals associated with cellular recovery — making proteins, cells moving and multiplying, inflammation settling, antioxidant enzymes being produced — are reported to become more active alongside it.

Its role differs from our existing light-based procedures

This clinic already offers light-based procedures such as IPL and laser toning. Quantum care is different: rather than resurfacing skin or breaking down pigment, its purpose is to create the conditions in which cells produce energy better. The same "light", but a different role.

How does it connect to our stem cell programmes?

Our stem cell programmes and Quantum care aim at the same point — cellular energy and regeneration. The methods differ. One adds material into the body; the other helps the cells you already have to work better, from outside.

Programme components

Care using light of specific wavelengths to support cellular energy production

This may suit you if

  • you have had a stem cell or surgical procedure and want the recovery period managed alongside it
  • fatigue lingers and you feel not quite as you were
  • surgery or injections feel daunting and you would rather start with a non-invasive approach
  • you would like to combine it with skin care such as IPL or laser toning
  • you want to work on age-related loss of resilience at the level of the cell

How it proceeds

  1. ConsultationWe review your current condition, any illnesses and the medicines you take.
  2. CheckWe look at whether any of the situations where this is unsuitable applies to you.
  3. PlanningWe set the order and spacing relative to your other procedures.
  4. The sessionCarried out without incision or injection.
  5. Follow-upWe watch your response and adjust the programme.

Please read this before you decide

The degree of effect and response varies with individual health, and the same result is not guaranteed for everyone. This programme is supportive care that assists recovery. It does not replace the standard treatment of any condition that requires diagnosis and treatment.

Please tell us at your consultation if any of these apply
  • you are pregnant or may be pregnant
  • you have been diagnosed with, or treated for, cancer
  • you use an implanted electronic medical device such as a pacemaker
  • you have a condition that makes you sensitive to sunlight, or take a medicine with that side effect
  • there is a wound, infection or marked inflammation in the area to be treated
  • you are under treatment for heart, liver or kidney disease
outro:
Frequently asked questions

"Quantum" sounds rather difficult.
It is a term from physics for the smallest packet of energy. It sounds difficult, but the content is simple. It means that the way light and energy act on cells has been applied in a clinical setting — and nothing beyond that.
Does it hurt?
There is no incision and no injection. During the session most people feel no more than warmth.
How many sessions do I need?
It depends on the purpose and your condition. We advise you individually at the consultation.
Can I have it together with a stem cell procedure?
Whether they can be combined, and in what order, is decided at your consultation.
How is it different from IPL or laser toning?
IPL and laser toning act directly on pigment or the skin surface. Quantum care does not apply that kind of stimulus; it is closer to helping cells build their own capacity to recover.
Will I feel the effect straight away?
Because it works by supporting the energy metabolism of cells, it is care that is repeated over a period while changes are observed. Immediate change is not guaranteed.
Can I have it right after another procedure?
This depends on the area and the state of recovery, so we set the timing at your consultation.
Is it covered by health insurance?
It is a non-covered item. We explain the cost in detail at your consultation.

Please note

The content of this page is general medical information. It does not guarantee a diagnosis or a treatment outcome for any individual. Results and responses may differ according to personal condition, and side effects are possible. Please always discuss the details with our medical team.
